# Verifier rules {#sec-app-verifier}

The verifier (`services/workers/ml_evaluation/llm_judge_evaluator.py`) accepts a quote only if every
fragment passes:

- *Normalization.* Unicode normalization; literal line-break escapes, markup escapes, footnote marks,
  emphasis markers and inline HTML removed; quotation marks and dashes unified; the result marks
  "(+)" and "(-)" turned into the words *positiv* and *negativ* (positive, negative); case folded; whitespace collapsed.
- *Fragments.* A quote is split at ellipses. Each fragment needs at least
  `{python} VER["min_tokens"]` tokens, or two tokens with `{python} VER["two_token_min_chars"]` letters
  together, and more than a norm citation. The whole quote needs `{python} VER["min_word_chars"]` word
  characters.
- *Matching.* Fragments with fewer than `{python} VER["short_fragment_tokens"]` tokens must match on
  word boundaries. Longer ones may match as a substring or token by token in order, with up to
  `{python} VER["max_skipped_answer_words"]` skipped answer words between quoted words and one missed
  quoted word per `{python} VER["one_miss_per_tokens"]`. Unprotected words of at least
  `{python} VER["typo_min_chars"]` letters may differ by one edit or a small inflection. Glued passages
  without an ellipsis are checked sentence by sentence.
- *Protected tokens.* Negations, result words and their antonyms (including every *un-* form),
  qualifiers such as *nur* (only) and *teilweise* (partly), Roman numerals and every token with a digit must match
  exactly. They may not be dropped, added, swapped or stepped over. Numbers never match part of a
  longer number.
- *Edges.* A match fails if a negation or a condition (*ob*, *wenn*, *falls*, *sofern*, *soweit*: whether, if, in case, provided, insofar)
  stands right before it in the same clause, or a negation, a negative result mark or a condition
  right after it in the same sentence.

```{=latex}
\FloatBarrier
```

# Validator checks {#sec-app-validator}

The validator checks every generated sheet before it is used. *Hard* checks fail an attempt and
return their messages to the model: the document structure and
every cross-reference; steps above `{python} num(GEN["max_step_be"], 0)` BE; steps above
`{python} num(GEN["two_bullets_above_be"], 0)` BE with a single requirement; requirements that can be met by an
absence or that are conditional; steps named as a result (except the finding after a taking of
evidence and the operative part of a judgment, *Tenor*); regular steps that depend on a step of an
alternative path;
forks whose steps depend on replaced steps;
a fork that replaces a whole section; and a path whose requirements repeat those of the replaced steps
(word overlap of at least `{python} num(GEN["duplicate_jaccard"], 1)`). *Soft* checks only log hints:
broader absence patterns; forks that replace exactly one step with one step; forks above
`{python} num(GEN["large_weichenstellung_be"], 0)` BE; near-duplicate requirements; requirements that only name something and are
shorter than `{python} GEN["bare_naming_min_words"]` words; a sheet on which most steps exceed
`{python} num(GEN["step_be_guidance"][1], 0)` BE; and rescaled sections in top-down allocation.

```{=latex}
\FloatBarrier
```

# Pipeline options not tested here {#sec-app-options}

The code supports the options below. The experiments in this paper do not vary them.

- *Weight elicitation.* The generator can state flat weights over all steps; shares per level, where
  each item states its percentage of the item above it (Roth's paradigm, Z2); or section totals first
  and then the steps inside (the D2 paradigm). Code normalizes all three. Every sheet in this paper
  uses flat weights.
- *Case preparation.* Code removes markup escapes and tables of contents from the case text and the
  reference solution and keeps footnotes.
- *Allocation detail.* Steps whose share falls below the minimum are set to it before the remainders
  are ranked, and the rest is apportioned again. Every other step then lands within one half point of
  its exact share, and weights that already sum to the total pass unchanged.
- *Merged view.* A second rendering merges consecutive steps of a section until a merged step reaches
  about `{python} num(GEN["merged_view_target_be"], 0)` BE, without crossing a focal group, a fork or
  an auxiliary-opinion marker. Totals do not change.
- *Rating unit.* The judge grades each step from 0 to `{python} JDG["rating_max"]` against the
  statutory grade definitions. A step grade maps back to BE at the middle of its band under the exam's
  key, with `{python} JDG["rating_max"]` points worth the full step. The weighted average of the step
  grades, Roth's aggregation, is reported next to it.
- *Two-judge mean.* The totals of two judges can be averaged.
- *Shown step scores.* The step scores shown to a reader are distributed from the rounded total by
  largest remainder, so that they add up to it.

```{=latex}
\FloatBarrier
```

# Designs for alternative solution paths {#sec-app-alternatives}

A dispute that changes only a result or its reasons (a local alternative) stays inside a step as an
outcome-neutral requirement, such as "discusses the dispute with the arguments of both sides; both results
defensible". A structural fork replaces named steps of the reference solution's path with the steps of each
alternative path, within the same budget. We compare three designs (E4):

- *A0, replace.* Only the reference solution's path is scored. The rendered sheet tells the judge to
  credit work on another defensible path on the replaced steps. This is the first iteration's design; it
  needs the step or rating unit, because a requirement of a replaced step describes that step's own
  requirement.
- *A1, branch, best path.* The judge scores the steps of every path; code counts the path with the
  most points.
- *A2, branch, declared path.* As A1, but code counts the path the judge declares the answer follows,
  backed by a verified quote; without one it counts the reference solution's path.

A1 and A2 come from the same call. A path counts as followed only if the answer argues it as its
defensibility requirements demand; a bare other result does not count.

```{=latex}
\FloatBarrier
```

```{python}
krows = [[NAME.get(m, m), f"{p:.3f}"] for m, p in sorted(COST["judge_call_usd"].items(), key=lambda kv: kv[1])]
krows.append("MIDRULE")
krows += [[f"Sheet: {NAME.get(m, m)}", f"{p:.2f}"] for m, p in sorted(COST["sheet_usd"].items(), key=lambda kv: kv[1])]
write_table(
    "tbl_costs",
    f"Planned cost in USD per judge call (about {COST['judge_call_tokens_in'] // 1000}k input and "
    f"{COST['judge_call_tokens_out'] // 1000}k output tokens) and per generated sheet, from pilot-measured "
    "tokens at catalog prices. Open-model sheets cost less than the value shown. \\pending{measured costs}",
    "tab:costs", ["Model", "USD"], krows, size=r"\footnotesize")
```

The program is planned at `{python} usd(COST["experiments_sum_usd"][0])` to
`{python} usd(COST["experiments_sum_usd"][1])` (Table \ref{tab:experiments}).

# Data statement {#sec-app-datastatement}

*D1.* The first-iteration corpus of `{python} V["n_exams"]` German exams and `{python} V["n_answers"]`
answers with blind human grades [@nagl2026bengerdata]. Exam texts are third-party material used under
the permissions documented for that corpus and are not redistributed. Human grades are pseudonymized.

*D2.* One police-law exam with its author's sheet and key, `{python} D2["d2a"]["n_scripts"]` graded
scripts (D2a) and `{python} D2["d2b"]["n_students"]` student submissions to a practice exam (D2b),
used with the students' consent for research. All texts are pseudonymized before any research call to
a model provider. The check found and removed `{python} D2["pii"]["student_name_lines_removed"]` line
with a student's name and `{python} D2["pii"]["examiner_headers_removed"]` examiner header;
`{python} D2["pii"]["grade_files_with_private_email"]` grade spreadsheets carried a private e-mail
address, which no derived file contains. The material stays private; only aggregate statistics are
published. \pending{who wrote the scripts and when, exam status, consent process, storage location and
deletion date}

*Z2.* Gregor Roth's grading sheet and workbook for a civil-law exam, without case, solution or
scripts. Private; described only by its structure.

*Model calls.* Every call records the model id, parameters, prompt hashes and the code version. For D1
we release aggregates; the per-call records are withheld for size.
\pending{owner: release the per-call records with the dataset release?}
